segments.text: What do you see as the largest bottleneck to 10xing enterprise adoption and making these models actually useful on the true eval of the customer?
Very simply put, it's evals. It's measurement.
You know, there's a lot more to say about that, but the bottom line is I think we have plenty of intelligence.
The line I draw in the sand is like, I think, Claude Sonnet 3.5, which also feels like a very quaint statement to make that makes me sound ancient.
Some people don't remember anything before Claude 4 at this point.
But back in my day, we had Sonnet 3.5, and that was an awesome upgrade.
And from then on, it's kind of felt like the models are good enough at a lot of really complex enterprise tasks and knowledge tasks much of the time.
The problem isn't the model being smarter.
You can take the world's smartest person in the world and sit them down at a desk and say, do work.
So I think the real challenge is describing what you want AI to do and knowing whether AI did it.
That's an eval task by and large.
If we get better at that, I think we will unlock huge amounts of AI value for enterprises.

If we don't get better at that, you could give me a model that is 10x smarter than Mythos and the world's smartest person without knowing what they're supposed to do and what it means to do a good job is still going to fail.
